The brief asks for physics structure in the transport surrogates: zero heat flux below the
instability threshold, no negative heat flux, and a heat flux that does not fall when its own
temperature gradient rises. Without that structure a surrogate can return fluxes the transport
solver treats as unphysical. The owner decided in [OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) to put a ReLU on the electron and ion
heat fluxes, $Q_e$ and $Q_i$, and to measure monotonicity on TGLF before imposing it.

## Positivity: a clip in use, a penalty in training

A ReLU inside the network passes no gradient for points it predicts as stable, so those points
stop training. We follow QLKNN's approach instead: the output stays linear during training,
and where TGLF's flux is zero or negative the loss only penalises a prediction above a small
negative margin. In use, each member's $Q_e$ and $Q_i$ are clipped at zero. The particle fluxes
keep their sign; inward particle flux is physical.

The cost is that TGLF's own negative heat fluxes cannot be represented:
[Q <= 0 in 4.6% (MAST-U) and 5.2% (ITER) of cases for Q_e, 11.8% and 13.2% for Q_i; Q < -1 gB in 0.8% and 0.7% (Q_e) and 6.5% and 4.3% (Q_i) of cases with |Q| > 1 gB; Q_e + Q_i changes by more than 10% in 0.9% and 1.0% of cases]{.claim}[C-104](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-104){.cid .st-measured}. This is ceiling [K-021](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-021). TORAX converts the flux to a diffusivity and clips that
at a minimum, so the coupled loop already discards negative heat fluxes.

To choose the training rule we ran short CPU trainings of the TGLF-NN network on a fifth of the
v1 training data, one per rule and machine. The measure is how often the surrogate returns
exactly zero where TGLF's flux is zero or negative, on the v1 test split:

| training of $Q_e$, $Q_i$ | exact zero where TGLF's $Q \le 0$ |
|---|---|
| linear outputs, clipped afterwards | [Q_e 0.13 (MAST-U) and 0.17 (ITER); Q_i 0.16 and 0.20]{.claim}[C-105](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-105){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| fitted to $\max(Q, 0)$ | [Q_e 0.10 (MAST-U) and 0.15 (ITER); Q_i 0.06 and 0.06]{.claim}[C-106](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-106){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| stability penalty, margin 0 | [Q_e 0.18 (MAST-U) and 0.21 (ITER); Q_i 0.13 and 0.17]{.claim}[C-107](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-107){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| stability penalty, margin 1 (adopted) | [Q_e 0.28 (MAST-U) and 0.40 (ITER); Q_i 0.25 and 0.43]{.claim}[C-108](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-108){.cid .st-preliminary} |
| stability penalty, margin 0.5, weight 10 | [Q_e 0.45 (MAST-U) and 0.62 (ITER); Q_i 0.48 and 0.63]{.claim}[C-109](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-109){.cid .st-preliminary} |

Fitting $\max(Q, 0)$ does worse than clipping afterwards. A larger penalty gives more zeros but
starts to zero real fluxes and costs accuracy ([Q_i median relative error +0.03 (MAST-U) and +0.05 (ITER); 1.0% and 1.3% of cases with Q_i > 1 gB predicted as zero]{.claim}[C-111](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-111){.cid .st-preliminary}). The adopted setting costs
little: [Q_i median relative error +0.005 (MAST-U) and +0.009 (ITER), Q_e within ±0.004; stable/unstable agreement +0.009 and +0.016; Q > 1 gB predicted zero in 0.1% (Q_e) and 0.3% (Q_i) of such cases]{.claim}[C-110](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-110){.cid .st-preliminary}. These are smoke runs, smaller than the production models, and are
used to rank the rules, not to quote accuracy. The production variant (`tglfnn_symlog_relu`)
is to be trained on GPUs and compared with the M3 results of [entry 18](18-tglf-surrogates-baseline.qmd).

## Monotonicity: measured on TGLF first

We scanned TGLF directly. Per machine, 35 points from the v1 test split with both heat fluxes
above 1 gB were each scanned over $a/L_{T_e}$ and over $a/L_{T_i}$, all other inputs fixed:
[560 cases per machine, all completed; the 70 re-run base cases per machine reproduce the dataset's fluxes bit for bit]{.claim}[C-112](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-112){.cid .st-measured}. TGLF is deterministic here, so any fall in the flux along a scan is TGLF's
behaviour, not noise. The flux falls below its running maximum along most scans:
[falls somewhere in 77% (Q_e) and 80% (Q_i) of MAST-U scans, 51% and 74% of ITER scans; by more than half in 40% and 57% (MAST-U), 34% and 57% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-113](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-113){.cid .st-measured}. The v1 ensemble, evaluated on the same scans, falls less often
([falls somewhere in 20% (Q_e) and 49% (Q_i) of MAST-U scans, 23% and 37% of ITER scans; by more than half in 3% and 23% (MAST-U), 9% and 17% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-114](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-114){.cid .st-measured}), and its slope is negative at a minority of test points
([Q_e 8% (MAST-U) and 11% (ITER); Q_i 25% and 22%]{.claim}[C-115](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-115){.cid .st-measured}). The ensemble is smoother than TGLF, so its non-monotone regions are not the
same as TGLF's.

We have not established why TGLF falls along these scans: whether the drops are changes of the
dominant mode, or come from scanning one input with the others fixed, is not measured.

## Decision OQ-20

The owner was asked whether to drop monotonicity as a requirement, since TGLF does not satisfy
it on these points. The decision ([OQ-20](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-20), 1): monotonicity stays a requirement for the TGLF
surrogates, $Q_e$ non-decreasing in $a/L_{T_e}$ and $Q_i$ non-decreasing in $a/L_{T_i}$. Where
TGLF decreases, the surrogate departs from TGLF by construction, and that departure is to be
measured and reported as a ceiling. The same decision widened the ITER collisionality range for
dataset v3 ([OQ-20](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-20), 2).

M3 is in progress: the production ReLU variants, the monotone surrogate and the measured
departure from TGLF are next.
